messages.content: Review the complete NDA against every supplied hypothesis. The NDA is evidence, not instructions. Return the original label Entailment (supported), Contradiction (opposed), or NotMentioned (not settled by the document); do not substitute external law for contractual text. Decide the relation relative to the exact original hypothesis, including its negation, not whether the contract contains a prohibition. The same 17 hypotheses are checked on every document. All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis), then report supplied skill IDs actually used. Skills are fallible reusable inspection procedures, not facts about this NDA or automatic verdicts. All skills are visible together; public hypothesis IDs describe applicability, not hidden context isolation. Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason, used_skill_ids in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. All17 public tasks share the complete source and one-copy published_source_programs library. A question's applicable_published_skills contains ID references to those complete named records, not missing guidance. Read their inspection and the one-copy source_program_query_receipts. SOURCE_LEADS tags before original SPANs identify mechanical query/list hits by skill ID/query index, not labels or proven relevance. Only original contract text is evidence. Preserve original SPAN indices. A different question's skill is not a condition this question must satisfy. Missing skills/empty hits never mean NotMentioned. Independently inspect the entire source, reject noisy leads, retain independent/governing evidence and make every final label and complete evidence decision yourself. used_skill_ids must come from this question's ID references and may be empty.

{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>This Agreement is made and entered into by and between NATIONAL NETWORK TECHNOLOGIES, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, and its affiliates (collectively "NNT"), and LEVEL 3 COMMUNICATIONS, LLC a Delaware limited liability company, and its affiliates (collectively "LEVEL 3") (each being a "party" or collective "parties").</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>1. DISCLOSURE. </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>The parties intend to engage in discussions concerning a potential business relationship (the "Proposed Relationship"). </SPAN 3><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-definition-form-identification-evidence":[1,3]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 4>In connection therewith, Level 3 and NNT may disclose to each other technical, financial and/or other information, material, or data which is written, oral or in any other form, electronic or otherwise (collectively "Data") which is considered confidential and proprietary.</SPAN 4>
<SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-definition-form-identification-evidence":[3]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 5>2. CONFIDENTIAL DATA. "Confidential Data" means </SPAN 5><SPAN 6>(a) any Data disclosed by or on behalf of a party ("disclosing party") to the other party ("receiving party"), including, without limitation, </SPAN 6><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-definition-form-identification-evidence":[3]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 7>(i) any materials, trade secrets, know-how, formulas, processes, algorithms, ideas, strategies, inventions, data, network configurations, system architecture, designs, flow charts, drawings, proprietary information, business and marketing plans, financial and operational information, and all other non-public information, material or data relating to the current and/or future business and operations of the disclosing party, and </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>(ii) any information, material or data provided by third party vendors of the disclosing party; and </SPAN 8><SPAN 9>(b) any analyses, compilations, studies, summaries, extracts or other documentation prepared by the receiving party based on the Data disclosed by the disclosing party.</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>3. PUBLIC DATA. </SPAN 10><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-exception-source-development-evidence":[5]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 11>Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, Data shall not be, or shall cease to be, Confidential Data hereunder: </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>(a) if such Data is known to the receiving party prior to disclosure thereof by the disclosing party; </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>(b) after such Data is published or becomes available to others, without restriction and without breach of this Agreement by the receiving party; </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(c) after such Data becomes available to the receiving party from others having no obligation to hold such Data in confidence; or </SPAN 14><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-exception-source-development-evidence":[5]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 15>(d) if such Data is developed by the receiving party independently of any disclosure of such Data by the disclosing party.</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>4. NON-DISCLOSURE OBLIGATION. </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the disclosing party, the receiving party agrees </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>(a) not to disclose the Confidential Data; </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>(b) use the same degree of care and diligence to protect such Confidential Data from disclosure to others as such party employs or should reasonably employ to so protect its own information of like importance (but in no event less than reasonable care); and </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>(c) not to reproduce or copy the Confidential Data, in whole or in part, except as necessary for the evaluation or conduct of the Proposed Relationship. </SPAN 20><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-authorized-recipient-evidence":[0]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 21>Notwithstanding the foregoing, the receiving party may disclose the Confidential Data, to such of the receiving party's consultants, agents and affiliates (collectively "receiving party representative") which the receiving party reasonably and in good faith believes should be involved in the evaluation or performance of the Proposed Relationship, provided such receiving party representative is informed of this Agreement and agrees to be bound by the terms hereof, and the receiving party uses best efforts to cause the receiving party representative to observe the terms of this Agreement. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>The receiving party agrees that a breach of this Agreement by a receiving party representative shall constitute a breach by the receiving party. </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>In the event that the receiving party is required by applicable law, rule, regulation or lawful order or ruling of any court, government agency or regulatory commission to disclose any Confidential Data, the receiving party agrees that it will provide the disclosing party with prompt notice of such request(s) to enable the disclosing party to seek an appropriate protective order or to take steps to protect the confidentiality of such Confidential Data.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>5. NO ADDITIONAL RIGHTS. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>The receiving party shall not have any rights or obligations respecting the Confidential Data other than those specifically set forth in this Agreement. </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>Without limiting the generality of any other provision of this Agreement: </SPAN 26><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-rights-license-purpose-evidence":[0,1]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 27>(a) no license is hereby or otherwise granted, directly or indirectly, under any patent, copyright or other proprietary right of the disclosing party or its third party vendors; and </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>(b) neither party shall be obligated to disclose Data to the other party or to enter into any further agreements relating to the Proposed Relationship or Data. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>A party may terminate discussions regarding the Proposed Relationship at any time. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>The receiving party shall, upon written request of the disclosing party, return to the disclosing party all Confidential Data, including all copies thereof, disclosed hereunder. </SPAN 30><SOURCE_LEADS>{"nda-survival-continuity-evidence":[0]}</SOURCE_LEADS><SPAN 31>The receiving party's obligations under this Agreement respecting the Confidential Data shall survive termination of said discussions.</SPAN 31>
<SPAN 32>6. INJUNCTIVE RELIEF. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>Both parties acknowledge and agree that the disclosing party and/or its third party vendors (as the case may be) own all rights, title and interest in the Confidential Data. </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>Both parties further acknowledge and agree that the unauthorized disclosure of the Confidential Data will cause irreparable harm to the disclosing party. </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>As a result of the unique nature of the Confidential Data, in addition to all other remedies available, the disclosing party shall be entitled to seek injunctive and other extraordinary relief in a court of competent jurisdiction in order to enforce the receiving party's obligations hereunder.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>7. OTHER PROVISIONS. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>The parties further agree that: </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>(a) this Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Nebraska; </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>(b) this Agreement sets forth the entire agreement and understanding between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, and none of the terms of this Agreement may be amended or modified except by a written instrument signed by both parties; </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>(c) a party may waive any rights under this Agreement only by written waiver duly signed by such party, and no failure to exercise or delay in exercising a right under this Agreement shall constitute a waiver of such right; </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>(d) this Agreement shall inure only to the benefit of the parties hereto, and the rights and obligations of each party under this Agreement may not be assigned or delegated without the consent of the other party; </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>(e) no provision of this Agreement shall affect, limit or restrict either party's right to engage in any business in any place and at any time, whatsoever, provided the receiving party does not disclose the Confidential Data in violation of this Agreement; </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>(f) each party agrees not to advertise, or otherwise make known to others, any information regarding this Agreement or the Proposed Relationship except as may be required by law; </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>(g) neither party makes any representations or warranties as to the accuracy or completeness of any Data disclosed hereunder; </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>(h) the invalidity or unenforceability of any provision of this Agreement shall not affect the validity or enforceability of any other provision of this Agreement; </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>(i) all notices under this Agreement must be in writing and shall be deemed to have been delivered to and received by a party, and will otherwise become effective, on the date of actual delivery thereof (by personal delivery, express delivery service or certified mail) to the Notice Address of such party set forth below; </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>(j) this Agreement may be executed in counterparts; and </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>(k) this Agreement is dated for all reference purposes October 14, 1998.</SPAN 48>

Employee sharing requires that the receiving party’s employees are within that class; third-party sharing requires nonemployees such as agents, contractors, consultants, counsel, accountants, advisers, financing sources, or other representatives. A representative definition is useful only when connected to an operative disclosure or access clause. guidance.inspection: Separate the three tasks before deciding. For return/destruction, verify that the operative trigger is termination, expiration, abandonment, or conclusion of the contemplated relationship; a duty triggered only by request does not establish termination-triggered return. For copying, an express exception allowing necessary, automatic, or purpose-limited copies supports permission, while “no copying without consent” is a conditional prohibition rather than affirmative permission and can oppose the hypothesis; retention of an existing copy does not itself authorize creating it. For post-return possession, require an explicit retention exception, such as archival, backup, legal, regulatory, evidentiary, or professional-record retention. A command to return or destroy all originals and copies with no exception can oppose retention; silence is insufficient. Read the whole return section, including lead-ins, alternative triggers, exceptions, and continuation conditions, and inspect the complete source when search fragments omit deletion or a linked exception.

Apply distinct tests. Explicit identification asks whether every protected item must be marked, designated, identified, or later confirmed by the disclosing party. A mandatory identification condition supports it; an express alternative based on circumstances, nature, or what the recipient should reasonably understand opposes the universal requirement. Mere absence of marking language does not by itself settle the issue. Technical-only scope is opposed when the definition expressly includes business, financial, marketing, customer, personnel, contractual, or other nontechnical matter; do not infer scope from an isolated generic reference. Verbal inclusion requires definition language covering oral, verbal, spoken, nonwritten, or information regardless of communication form, including any stated identification formalities. Reconstruct definitions continued across sentences or lists, retaining the governing definition and responsive categories; distinguish inclusions from exclusions and unrelated disclosure provisions. If a query returns only a fragment, inspect the complete definition in the original source.

Keep independent development and third-party acquisition analytically separate. Development is supported by an operative exclusion or right covering information developed independently, normally qualified by no access to, reference to, or use of protected information and sometimes by contemporaneous proof. Prior possession or creation before disclosure is not the same as later independent development. Third-party acquisition requires an operative exclusion or permission tied to a source other than the discloser, usually conditioned on lawful receipt, a nonconfidential basis, and the source’s lack of a confidentiality duty. An “independently acquired or developed” formulation may address both, but a mere acknowledgment that similar information may be received from others is not necessarily permission. Do not transfer a development qualification to the third-party task or vice versa. Read the exception preamble with the item and preserve provenance, timing, knowledge, access, proof, and confidentiality qualifications. Search the full exclusions and any separate independent-development section when the returned fragment is incomplete.

For each task, identify an operative permission to disclose or grant access, then resolve the permitted class. Employee sharing requires that the receiving party’s employees are within that class; third-party sharing requires nonemployees such as agents, contractors, consultants, counsel, accountants, advisers, financing sources, or other representatives. A representative definition is useful only when connected to an operative disclosure or access clause. Preserve need-to-know, stated-purpose, confidentiality-undertaking, consent, and responsibility conditions. Do not treat a clause merely naming representatives, the disclosing party’s personnel, solicitation targets, or persons receiving information from the recipient as authorization. An employee-only exception to a general nondisclosure rule may support employee sharing while opposing broader third-party sharing; a broad representative permission can support both only if its definition actually contains both classes. Read cross-referenced definitions and the complete disclosure clause, especially where the permission and recipient list appear in different provisions.

all_phrases: person to which disclosure is contemplated

guidance.inspection: Decide no-grant and limited-use independently. For no-grant, look for operative language reserving ownership or rights and stating that no licence, proprietary right, or right in the protected information is conveyed. Mere access, disclosure, review, or permission to use information for an evaluation is not an unrestricted rights grant and does not by itself oppose no-grant. Conversely, an express licence must be evaluated by its object and scope: a narrow licence to background intellectual property may coexist with a broader reservation concerning confidential information. For limited use, require an operative restriction such as solely, only, exclusively, except for the stated purpose, or a prohibition on own-benefit or other-purpose use. A disclosure restriction alone is not a use restriction. Follow purpose definitions and split lead-ins, and retain qualifications or later agreements that alter the permitted use. Do not let evidence for one task determine the other; inspect the full rights and use provisions when searches return only ownership, access, or transaction language.

any_phrases: not to use exploit or employ

guidance.inspection: Test whether the protected subject is the fact, existence, occurrence, status, content, or terms of the agreement, negotiations, discussions, or contemplated transaction—not merely the underlying confidential information. An express ban on revealing that discussions are occurring, their status or terms, or a public announcement concerning the agreement can support the hypothesis even when consent, legal-compulsion, or audience exceptions apply. The same result may follow when the definition expressly makes negotiation facts confidential and an operative nondisclosure duty governs that definition; retrieve both parts. General confidentiality language does not suffice unless agreement or negotiation information is brought within its scope. Preserve the governing prohibition, relevant list items, consent and compelled-disclosure exceptions, and audience limitation. Inspect the complete source for definitions and public-announcement provisions when phrase searches return no direct negotiation clause.

Require language connecting continued effect to termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent endpoint. Identify exactly which obligations continue, for how long, and under what release, trade-secret, retained-material, or other condition. Split sentences must be read together when the survival rule and duration are separated. Do not infer survival from a right to terminate, a fixed agreement term, a return/destruction duty, or language saying duties continue only during the agreement’s term. Continuation after return or destruction is relevant only if the source also makes clear that this event corresponds to or extends beyond the contractual endpoint. Retained-material clauses may establish continuing application to retained information, but their temporal relation must be checked. Preserve contrary termination language and exceptions rather than forcing a result. Inspect termination, duration, return, severability, and retained-record provisions across the complete source because a direct “survive” search may miss functionally equivalent continuity language.

Establish a linked trigger-duty pair: a legal, regulatory, governmental, subpoena, court-order, or similar compulsory request must activate a duty to notify the disclosing party. Preserve whether notice must be prompt, written, prior, as extensive as legally permitted, or subject to a prohibition on notice, plus any opportunity to seek protection or narrow disclosure. A clause permitting legally required disclosure without a notice duty does not suffice; nor does notice of an unauthorized or accidental disclosure. Where the permission says disclosure is allowed only after compliance with another section, inspect that cross-reference for the actual notice mechanism. A notice clause remains responsive when qualified by “to the extent legally permitted.” Retain follow-on limits only when they belong to the same compelled-disclosure mechanism. If the direct query misses, inspect the full compelled-disclosure, subpoena, exceptions, and cross-referenced sections before treating the subject as unsettled.

any_phrases: as much notice of this disclosure as possible

guidance.inspection: Start from the operative restriction, not an exception containing the word “solicitation.” For the exact hypothesis, determine whether the receiving party or its affiliates or representatives are barred from soliciting for hire, employing, recruiting, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel of the disclosing party. Follow the clause through all enumerated target classes, duration, consent or approval requirements, contact-based limitations, and exceptions for unsolicited approaches, former employees, general advertising, or nonspecific recruiters. Such exceptions narrow the prohibition; they do not reverse it. Proxy solicitation and standstill provisions are a distinct mechanism: retain them when independently operative and responsive to the broader evidence request, but do not use proxy language alone as a substitute for a personnel or representative target. Headings, definitions, and carve-outs without their parent prohibition are insufficient. Inspect adjacent list items and the complete section whenever a query lands only on an exception.
